findings.summary: When VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is unset, main.tsx renders `<App />` bare (no ClerkProvider). WelcomeRoute then unconditionally mounts `<ClerkOtpPanel />` at line 890 for the fresh-lane state — but ClerkOtpPanel calls `useSignIn()` at line 92, and useSignIn calls `useAssertWrappedByClerkProvider('useSignIn')` (@clerk/clerk-react/dist/index.js:1305) which THROWS `Error: useSignIn can only be used within the <ClerkProvider /> component.` The 'shell renders + fallbacks operable' claim in the main.tsx comment is false — the fresh-lane branch crashes the entire login screen before any fallback link renders.
findings.evidence: main.tsx:13-27 conditionally wraps ClerkProvider only when CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is truthy. WelcomeRoute.tsx:880-890 mounts <ClerkOtpPanel /> for the fresh-lane state without any provider-availability guard. @clerk/shared/dist/runtime/react/index.js:99-104 throws `"useSignIn can only be used within the <ClerkProvider /> component."` when the ClerkInstanceContext is absent. ClerkOtpPanel.tsx has no error boundary above the useSignIn call.
findings.reproduce: Unset VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (or leave it empty for a preview build) → `npm run dev` → open the app → welcome flow throws before rendering. Console: `useSignIn can only be used within the <ClerkProvider /> component.` Screen: React error boundary or blank white.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the ClerkOtpPanel mount on the presence of ClerkProvider — either (a) pass a boolean prop from main.tsx into App → WelcomeRoute so the fresh-lane collapses to LC-ID + Whop text links only when the provider is absent, OR (b) surface a synthetic 'sign-in temporarily unavailable' state in ClerkOtpPanel BEFORE the useSignIn call (e.g. read `window.__LC_CLERK_ENABLED__` set alongside the AppTree branch in main.tsx), OR (c) make the ClerkOtpPanel component split — one wrapper reads the context flag, the inner component calls useSignIn only when the flag is on.

findings.summary: After `attemptFirstFactor` succeeds but returns `status: 'needs_second_factor'` (Clerk MFA enabled on the account) or `'needs_new_password'` (Clerk password-reset flow) the code shows a single generic 'Sign-in incomplete · retry from the top' toast and resets to the identifier phase — creating an infinite loop for MFA-enabled users who will never be able to sign in. Same for the 'needs_new_password' path where a returning user with a password-reset requirement can never progress. This is the exact silent-empty-render family: happy-path assumption ('complete' only) with a friendly-looking fallback that silently strands the user forever.
findings.evidence: SignInStatus enum @clerk/shared/dist/types/index.d.ts:3195 = 'needs_identifier' | 'needs_first_factor' | 'needs_second_factor' | 'needs_new_password' | 'complete'. ClerkOtpPanel.tsx:207 only branches on `status !== 'complete'` and drops to the identifier phase. There is no MFA UI, no password-reset UI, no telemetry step distinguishing MFA-required from unknown-error.
findings.reproduce: Enable MFA on any Clerk user in the connected instance (or set a temporary password-reset requirement) → complete first factor → the Verify button will report 'Sign-in incomplete · retry from the top' and dump the user back to email/phone entry, indefinitely.
findings.suggested_fix: At minimum, emit a distinct telemetry step for `attempt.status === 'needs_second_factor'` and render a copy line that says 'This account requires 2FA · sign in on the web at account.liquidclips.app' pointing at the LC-ID text-link fallback. Same treatment for 'needs_new_password'. Even if MFA is off on the current Clerk instance today, this is a P0 because ANY user who enables it later (or if MFA is turned on account-wide by the org) becomes permanently locked out. Also emit `logLoginStep('clerk_verify_needs_2fa', ...)` so the funnel captures the loss.

findings.summary: The Clerk exchange path calls `setJwt(license_jwt)` (sync, localStorage-only) but never mirrors the license JWT into the macOS Keychain via `setJwtKeychainForAuthAction()`. Every other authenticated entry point does mirror — activation.ts:424-429 does it right after setJwt as a fire-and-forget. Missing this mirror means: on the Tauri desktop build, a webview storage wipe on Vite bundle swap / quota purge silently signs the Clerk-authenticated user out on next launch even though 'sign-in worked.' The IG-014 mirror is the explicit auth-action allowlist Clerk sign-in should be a member of.
findings.evidence: ClerkOtpPanel.tsx:268 `setJwt(j.license_jwt);` — no follow-up import to setJwtKeychainForAuthAction. authStorage.ts:76-85 sets memoryCache + localStorage only. activation.ts:406 setJwt + 424-429 explicit keychain mirror is the pattern. IG-014 allowlist explicitly names 'sign-in' as one of the six approved auth actions.
findings.reproduce: Sign in via Clerk OTP → grep webview localStorage for `lc.license.jwt.v1` (present). Quit + wipe localStorage (or trigger the well-known Tauri webview cache purge). Reopen the app → user is signed out even though the Keychain would have held the token had the mirror been called.
findings.suggested_fix: After the successful `setJwt(j.license_jwt)` on line 268, add the same pattern as activation.ts:424-429: `void import('../../lib/authStorage').then(mod => mod.setJwtKeychainForAuthAction(j.license_jwt)).catch(...)` — fire-and-forget mirror to the Keychain so the JWT survives webview storage resets.

findings.summary: Exchange step reads `window.Clerk?.session?.getToken?.()` directly from the isomorphic global instead of `useAuth().getToken`. Two problems: (1) The Clerk 5.x internal `session` may not be synchronously readable right after `setActive` — the SDK's own `createGetToken` (dist/index.js:1209-1216) awaits `clerkLoaded(isomorphicClerk)` before touching session, protecting against exactly this race. (2) Reaching into `window.Clerk` bypasses the SDK's typing + the loaded gate; if a future major version renames the global or slots the session behind a getter, this call silently returns null and the flow surfaces 'Session token missing · retry sign-in' as if the user did something wrong.
findings.evidence: ClerkOtpPanel.tsx:229-236 `const w = window as unknown as { Clerk?: { session?: { getToken?: ... } } }; const token = await w.Clerk?.session?.getToken?.();`. Compare with @clerk/clerk-react/dist/index.js:1209-1216 `createGetToken = (isomorphicClerk) => { return async (options) => { await clerkLoaded(isomorphicClerk); if (!isomorphicClerk.session) return null; return isomorphicClerk.session.getToken(options); }` — the loaded-await is the safety this file bypasses.
findings.reproduce: Force-slow the network + call setActive → immediately call `window.Clerk.session.getToken()` in the same tick. On a slow-loading Clerk instance the session field may resolve after the promise chain returns.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the window-poking with `const { getToken } = useAuth();` at the top of the component and call `getToken()` inside handleVerify. useAuth already asserts ClerkProvider (which is inherent to the fix for P0-F01 above) and internally awaits clerkLoaded — no race, no fragile global typing.

findings.summary: The 'supported first factor not found' path shows a friendly message and returns — but the underlying signIn resource is left mid-flight (`create` succeeded, no `prepareFirstFactor` fired, no session cleanup). The next click of Send code creates a NEW signIn resource which shadows the abandoned one; Clerk's SignIn resource has a `_authRequestManager` inside that MAY queue transitions. This is unlikely to bite in practice but it's the exact pattern where a fresh install with a soft-verified-only account can double-consume rate limits + surface confusing 'too many attempts' errors upstream. Also no telemetry step distinguishes 'factor unavailable' from 'send failed'.
findings.evidence: ClerkOtpPanel.tsx:130-147 · `signIn.create` runs, then if the requested factor isn't in `supportedFirstFactors`, we setErr + return without emitting a distinct telemetry step. logLoginStep('clerk_send_code_failed') is only reached on catch. `clerk_send_code_succeeded` is only reached after prepareFirstFactor. The unsupported-factor branch is invisible in the funnel.
findings.reproduce: Sign in with an account whose primary factor is password only → this path runs → user sees 'This account can't sign in with an email code' but the funnel row is missing → HQ ships thinking Clerk is silent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `logLoginStep('clerk_send_code_failed', { kind, err: 'factor_unavailable' })` on the return path so the funnel captures this drop-off. Widen the LoginStep union OR reuse `clerk_send_code_failed` with a specific ctx.err code as done for the catch.

findings.summary: The `SignInResourceLike` inline interface + double `unknown as` casts fabricate a hidden assumption: 'we know the API surface stays this shape.' The comment says 'stable across 5.x per node_modules dump' — but @clerk/shared/types re-exports the real `SignInResource` interface at line 3777. The 'don't pin @clerk/types as devDependency' rationale is thin — `@clerk/shared` is already a transitive dep (pinned by @clerk/clerk-react ^5.61.8) and its types are already on disk. Casting away the real type loses editor autocomplete on `supportedFirstFactors`, the exhaustive SignInStatus enum (which would have caught P0-F02), and the specific PrepareFirstFactorParams shape.
findings.evidence: ClerkOtpPanel.tsx:22-45 inline interface + comment 'Rather than pin a new devDependency, inline the minimum-viable shapes'. `@clerk/shared/dist/types/index.d.ts:3777-3809` exports `SignInResource`, `SignInStatus`, `SignInFirstFactor`, `PrepareFirstFactorParams` — already installed under desktop-2/node_modules by virtue of @clerk/clerk-react depending on @clerk/shared. No new devDependency required to import them, just `import type { SignInResource } from '@clerk/shared/types'` or similar path.
findings.suggested_fix: Import the real `SignInResource`/`SignInStatus`/`SignInFirstFactor` types (or their re-exports from `@clerk/clerk-react`'s public entry). Drop the fabricated interface + the `unknown as` casts. tsc will catch a mishandled status branch (P0-F02) for free.

findings.summary: Exchange fail path logs `snippet: body.slice(0, 120)` — safe against LC JWT leaks (backend returns license_jwt only on 200 per contract), but a 500 with a Python traceback body could still surface backend internals into telemetry. logLoginStep POSTs to /telemetry/login-step, which lands in a public-facing HQ table. Better to strip the snippet to a short hash or omit the body entirely and rely on the status code for triage.
findings.evidence: ClerkOtpPanel.tsx:249 `const body = await r.text().catch(() => '');` line 259 `logLoginStep('clerk_exchange_failed', { status: r.status, snippet: body.slice(0, 120) });`. junior-backend/app/routes/auth_clerk_exchange.py:233 `except (jwt.InvalidTokenError, Exception) as e: raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, 'session token invalid')` — expected path emits terse strings, but a truly unexpected 5xx from any dependency (httpx timeout, DB error) can carry longer detail.
findings.reproduce: Force the backend to raise an unhandled exception (temporarily) → snippet in telemetry payload will contain FastAPI's default error body.
findings.suggested_fix: Change `snippet: body.slice(0, 120)` to `snippet_len: body.length` (or drop it) — status code + attempt count is enough for HQ triage; body is signal-poor and comes from unknown-trust origin.

findings.summary: Primary submit button text swap ('Verify' → 'Verifying…' → 'Signing you in…') has no aria-live announcement + no aria-label to keep the accessible name stable. Screen readers may re-focus / re-announce as the button label mutates during an active gesture, which some AT stacks treat as a fresh element. Minor a11y polish gap.
findings.evidence: ClerkOtpPanel.tsx:349-353 the button text renders three variants based on phase without a fixed `aria-label`.
findings.reproduce: VoiceOver + submit valid code → observe re-announcement on each state flip.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `aria-label="Verify code"` (fixed) to the submit button; keep visible text dynamic for sighted users. Or wrap the label swap in `aria-live="polite"`.
